reading.a: The announcement said 40 of 100 contacts; the company's own slide says 32, and those are contacts that start with the software, not ones it finished.
reading.b: A customer account contacted care 7 times a year in 2021 and about 3 times in 2026; the software agents arrived late in that fall.

slide.note: T-Mobile's slide: [[{v}]] served by an AI agent

rest.derivation: release value minus slide value; drawn, not printed as a number

overlap.note: drawn on the same {t} to compare; whether the {a} include the {b} isn't published
overlap.why: The 40 comes from a press release, the 32 from an investor slide. Drawing the 32 inside the 40 on the same 100 is the figure's choice, made to compare them; the note says that nobody published whether the 40 include the 32.

start.note: that is: they start with the software

finished.note: how many of these [[{v}]] the software finished: T-Mobile does not say

strip.note: A ruler is one year for one customer account; one dot is one contact. Positions are even spacing derived from the yearly value, not dates of real contacts.

points.note: about one every four months; [[{v}]] is an average

event.before: first point almost three years before the agents

causes.block: T-Mobile also names: problems removed before customers call; customers using the app
